profile.reading:
This facility sits at 15 Enterprise Avenue North, Secaucus, New Jersey 07094, off the Lincoln Tunnel corridor, roughly 14 miles from Newark Airport. Its OSM record labels it "NYC3," but Csquare's own current New York/New Jersey market page names the Secaucus facility "EWR5," alongside Weehawken (EWR2) and Piscataway (EWR3); "NYC3" does not appear anywhere on Csquare's current site or in its SEC filings, so this profile treats EWR5 as the operator-confirmed code for this address and flags "NYC3" as a legacy or third-party label rather than resolving definitively which predecessor company, Cyxtera or Evoque, may have originated it. Csquare (formerly branded Centersquare, launched April 2024 by Brookfield Infrastructure to combine Cyxtera, acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy for $775 million in a deal completed January 2024, and Evoque, AT&T's divested data center business under Brookfield since 2019) went public via IPO on NASDAQ in July 2026 at $21.00 per share. Csquare's own spec page states 59,572 square feet of raised floor at EWR5, closely matching its SEC Form S-1 property table figure of 59,407 square feet for "New Jersey-EWR5_A," 80.6 percent leased and Csquare-owned as of March 31, 2026. Csquare states 26.3 megawatts of utility power, 11.6 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 16 megawatts of generator capacity for this site, with SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001 compliance certifications. Csquare does not name a power utility or year-opened date.

Secaucus and the broader Hudson County, New Jersey data center corridor have developed as a lower-cost alternative to Manhattan proper while retaining direct fiber connectivity into the city's core carrier hotels via the Lincoln Tunnel corridor, a positioning shared by Csquare's nearby Weehawken (EWR2) and Piscataway (EWR3) sites. Csquare's SEC S-1 discloses 389 megawatts of total sellable power capacity across its full 64-facility, 21-market portfolio as of March 31, 2026, making the New York/New Jersey market, with three separate Csquare-branded sites, one of the company's more concentrated metro footprints in this dataset.

Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-03, batch 95 (Centersquare): operator market page found a renamed facility code, NYC3 in this registry versus EWR5 on the current market page, utility power and raised floor sqft applied under that likely but unconfirmed match, research_status upgraded from exhausted to complete, no address applied.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to Centersquare. This session found that centersquaredc.com, the legacy domain matching this registry entire Centersquare operator bucket naming, now issues a live redirect to www.csquare.com, the operator current domain, confirmed directly this session. Csquare own site states it owns and operates data centers built over decades by developing, acquiring, integrating, and operating advanced data centers, without giving a specific founding or rebrand date on the pages fetched this session. Csquare own site, fetched this session, lists corporate headquarters at 3100 Olympus Blvd, Suite 510, Coppell, TX 75019, and states a current portfolio of 80 total data centers, about 3.5 million square feet, more than 500 MW of power capacity, and more than 36,000 cross connects, across 15 North American markets plus London. On at least two Csquare pages fetched this session, a customer facing portal link pointed to evoquedcs.my.site.com, suggesting some relationship to Evoque Data Center Solutions, though this session found no page stating the exact nature of that relationship, such as whether Centersquare or Csquare is a direct rebrand of Evoque or a separate successor. Separately, this registry also carries an unrelated Cyxtera operator bucket, not part of this batch, already documented by an earlier pass in this registry as tracing to the same May 2017 CenturyLink data center divestiture discussed in this session own Lumen Technologies research, and as acquired by Cologix in 2023 per Cologix own site. This session found no evidence connecting that Cyxtera and Cologix history to the Centersquare, Csquare, or Evoque names researched for this batch, so the two threads are treated as distinct and unconfirmed to be related. This registry also carries a separate Csquare operator bucket, not part of this batch, whose name is now confirmed by the redirect evidence above to very likely be the same current brand as the Centersquare bucket this batch covers, though this session did not merge or rename either bucket, flagging this as an open duplicate operator naming question for a future dedicated pass rather than resolving it unilaterally. This row is named in the registry as Centersquare NYC3 Data Center, in Secaucus, NJ. The operator own current market page for New York and New Jersey, fetched this session, does not use the code NYC3 anywhere, and instead describes a Secaucus facility under the code EWR5, off the Lincoln Tunnel and 14 miles from Newark Airport, stating 26.3 MW of utility power and 59,572 square feet of raised floor, with no street address published on that page. Given the matching city, this session treats EWR5 as very likely the current operator code for the same building this registry recorded under the older NYC3 code, without independent proof the two codes refer to one identical building, and flags the code change itself as a discrepancy for a future researcher.

reading.body:
Centersquare NYC3 in Secaucus publishes no total capacity figure, but the operator's current market page lists this facility under the code EWR5 with 26.3 MW of utility power and 59,572 square feet of raised floor. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 26.3 MW of IT load is roughly 660 racks, though this figure assumes all utility power reaches the compute layer and reflects only what the operator has disclosed. The facility ranks sixth among New Jersey's mapped data centers by published megawatts, though only five facilities in the state publish capacity figures at all.

The site sits in Secaucus, 14 miles west of Newark Airport and accessible from the Lincoln Tunnel, placing it in the densest metro market on the US East Coast but not in a data center cluster itself. New Jersey's total published capacity across all operators is 111.3 MW, so this single facility represents roughly 24 percent of the state's disclosed power. The state has 48 mapped facilities in this registry, the vast majority of which publish no specifications.

The operator's certification status for this facility is not published. The research notes indicate a possible code change from NYC3 to EWR5 under the same operator's current branding, but no independent verification has confirmed these refer to the identical building. The operator's portfolio across North America totals more than 500 MW, so this one campus is a small fraction of their capacity.
